record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Matrix Theory Arising in Linear Systems and Control
record.original_question: For the decentralized static controller with block-diagonal gains u_i(t) = K_i y_i(t) across r feedback channels, determine when there exist gains K_1, ..., K_r such that the closed-loop matrix A + sum_i B_i K_i C_i is stable. The source frames this as the decentralized analogue of centralized output-feedback stabilization and states that the available theory is incomplete.

evidence.quote: For this problem the objective is to determine whether K_1, ..., K_r exist such that the closed-loop dynamics matrix A + sum_i B_i K_i C_i is stable.
Although some results have been obtained for this problem [3], the theory is far from complete.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $A \in \mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$, and for $i=1,\dots,r$ let $B_i \in \mathbb{R}^{n\times m_i}$ and $C_i \in \mathbb{R}^{p_i\times n}$ be given matrices. Consider the linear time-invariant system
$$\dot x(t) = A x(t) + \sum_{i=1}^{r} B_i u_i(t), \qquad y_i(t) = C_i x(t), \quad i=1,\dots,r,$$
together with the decentralized static output-feedback control law
$$u_i(t) = K_i\, y_i(t), \qquad K_i \in \mathbb{R}^{m_i \times p_i}, \quad i=1,\dots,r.$$
The resulting closed-loop dynamics matrix is
$$A_{\mathrm{cl}}(K_1,\dots,K_r) \;=\; A + \sum_{i=1}^{r} B_i K_i C_i.$$
A square real matrix is called (Hurwitz) stable if all of its eigenvalues have strictly negative real part.

Problem. Give verifiable necessary and sufficient conditions on the data $(A, B_1,\dots,B_r, C_1,\dots,C_r)$ for the existence of gain matrices $K_1,\dots,K_r$ such that $A_{\mathrm{cl}}(K_1,\dots,K_r)$ is stable. Equivalently, characterize the class of multi-channel triples $\{(A,B_i,C_i)\}_{i=1}^{r}$ that are stabilizable by decentralized static output feedback with block-diagonal gain structure.
artifact.status_search_result: Decentralized static output-feedback stabilization remains an open problem in control theory. Even the centralized static output-feedback stabilization problem (r=1) does not have a tractable necessary and sufficient verifiable characterization; only sufficient LMI/BMI conditions, iterative algorithms, and partial characterizations (e.g., via fixed modes for the decentralized case) are known. No general computationally verifiable necessary and sufficient condition has been established.

status_evidence.title: Static Output Feedback Stabilization: A story of people and matrices
status_evidence.snippet: Survey describing static output feedback stabilization as a long-standing problem with only partial results and computationally hard characterizations.
status_evidence.claim: The static output-feedback stabilization problem (centralized case) is widely surveyed as an open and computationally challenging problem; the decentralized variant inherits and extends this difficulty.

status_evidence.title: Robust decentralized static output feedback
status_evidence.snippet: Provides only sufficient conditions for decentralized static output feedback via modified Lyapunov equations.
status_evidence.claim: Available results for decentralized static output-feedback stabilization provide sufficient (not necessary and sufficient) conditions.
